instruction: Maximize the VLC window without entering fullscreen mode.

command: import pyautogui; import time; pyautogui.click({SCREEN_WIDTH_HALF}, {SCREEN_HEIGHT_HALF}); time.sleep(0.5);

metadata.explanation: Task requires maximizing VLC window (not fullscreen). Agent can double-click title bar or click maximize button. Custom getter compares window size to screen size: maximized = close to screen size but with margins for decorations, fullscreen = exact match. Metric verifies is_maximized=True and is_fullscreen=False.
metadata.verification: Maximized window: close to screen size with margins (±50px width, ±100px height for decorations). Fullscreen: exact screen size match. Getter uses get_vm_window_size and get_vm_screen_size.

llm_judge_reasons: Evaluator correctly distinguishes maximized from fullscreen by comparing window size to screen size with appropriate margins
Getter logic properly extracts both window dimensions and screen dimensions using get_vm_window_size() and get_vm_screen_size()
Fullscreen detection is correct: exact match between window and screen dimensions
Maximized detection logic: window size approximately equals screen size with margins for decorations (±50px width, ±100px height)
The getter correctly returns is_maximized=True only when maximized AND not fullscreen, satisfying instruction requirement 'without entering fullscreen mode'
Metric function correctly compares is_maximized field from result with expected value
Complete coverage: both requirements verified (maximize window + not fullscreen)
Good error handling: returns default false values on exceptions
llm_judge_fix_suggestions: Hardcoded margin values (±50px width, ±100px height) may be too restrictive for some desktop environments with larger window decorations - consider making margins configurable or more generous (e.g., ±100px for both dimensions)

Consider adding a small sleep/wait in postconfig to ensure window state is fully settled after maximize operation, though this is likely not critical since maximize operations are typically synchronous
